event: Before dawn the Honeycomb's ovens wake Elsie in her attic; the room smells of bread.
It is her Naming day; she lies under the sloped ceiling, too nervous and happy to stay in bed.
She waters her plants on the sill, Mrs Pennywhistle, Sunny, Doris and Captain, wishing each luck.
She washes at the basin, cold water on her bare small breasts, and laughs at the shock of it.
She laces the cream halter up the front, buckles her belt, and pins her flower clip twice.
Downstairs the baker, floury to the elbows, kisses both her cheeks and wishes her luck.
Elsie tells the baker she hopes for a healer's class, like her mother's on the caravan roads.
She walks the canals toward the lakeshore through the dawn mist, humming without knowing it.
Flower sellers set out buckets, lamplighters' boats douse the lanterns, and the Mere is silver.
Hours early, she wanders the waking city, then joins the line at the white Hall of Naming.
She chats with the shaking boy ahead of her, learns his sister's name, and promises he'll be fine.
The priestess calls names; windows open in the air, Baker, Bargeman, Scribe, and the hall claps.
The priestess calls Elsie Fairweather, and she steps alone into the silver circle in the floor.
The window opens above her, large enough for the whole hall to read: her name, and Enthraller.
The hall goes silent; somebody drops a hymn book, and the line behind her steps back as one.
Elsie reads it twice and tells the priestess, "Oh! That sounds like a lot of responsibility."
Her own window opens when she wishes it: level 1, Captivate, Tether. No healer's anything.
The priestess, voice shaking, tells her she must go to the guild hall today; it is the law.
Walking out, Elsie hears the whispers: Vesper Locke, the War of Strings. Her smile wobbles once.
On the hall steps she hugs her satchel and decides the class will just have to be kind.
At the guild hall on Brightwater Square, Elsie queues to register like everyone else.
The clerk asks two lanterns for the fee; Elsie pays, and the clerk's pen stops at her class.
The clerk goes up the stairs at a near run; the hall's chatter dies, and adventurers stare.
The guildmaster, a grey-haired swordswoman, comes down and asks to see Elsie's window.
Elsie shows it gladly, and asks whether she has filled the form in wrong.
The guildmaster registers her an F-rank Enthraller under the Strings Accord, and sends for a Warden.
From behind the charcoal door the guildmaster calls Cora: Corisande Vane, tall, grey-eyed, stern.
Cora sets out the Accord in a flat voice: no skill on anyone unwilling, unless it saves a life.
Every skill Elsie uses, Cora will write in her black ledger and report; and she can sever any bond.
Elsie takes both Cora's hands, thanks her for coming, and asks what she likes in her tea.
Cora draws her hands back, colour high on her cheekbones, and says that is not relevant.
The clerk stamps a copper rank tag with Elsie's name; Elsie kisses it and hangs it at her belt.
Elsie asks how one finds a party; Cora says the guild licenses a dungeon only to three or more.
At the party board, every slate Elsie walks up to is wiped or turned away before she reaches it.
One party leader tells her plainly that no party in Lanternmere will take an Enthraller.
Elsie thanks her anyway, and Cora writes something down.
In the board's bottom corner, the Leftovers, a copper-haired girl is chalking her own name.
Tamsin Reyes, freckled, chalks Berserker, E-rank, and introduces her axe, Margery, before herself.
Her knuckle wraps are bloody; the Copper Hounds dropped her this morning, after she broke an arm.
Elsie kneels with her satchel, unwraps Tamsin's split knuckles, cleans them and binds them fresh.
Tamsin, braced for a lecture, gets a hum instead, and Elsie's soft thumb stroking her wrist.
Tamsin looks down at her: glossy pink lips, the halter laced over small breasts, bare waist.
Tamsin, who likes girls and says so loudly, cannot find a single word.
Tamsin heard the hall whisper Enthraller; does Elsie know Tamsin hurts friends in her Frenzy?
Elsie says she knows what she is too, and the board hasn't been kind to either of them.
Elsie asks Tamsin into her party; Tamsin laughs, then sees she means it, and says yes.
Elsie hugs her hard, face in Tamsin's neck; Tamsin's arms hang a moment, then close around her.
A pop and a puff of green smoke come from the far end of the corner, and a wail.
A small blonde girl flaps at a fizzing vial, braids singed, goggles askew: Tilly Brandt.
Tilly apologises before anyone speaks: the College threw her out, her brews explode, she's sorry.
Her slip on the board reads: Alchemist, F-rank, will clean up after myself, sorry in advance.
Elsie wipes the soot from Tilly's cheek with her thumb, and Tilly stops talking mid-word.
Tilly stares at Elsie's mouth, goes scarlet to the ears, and starts talking twice as fast.
Elsie owns up that she's the Enthraller the whole hall is whispering about; Tilly only blinks.
Elsie asks her to join; Tilly asks if she's sure three times, and Tamsin says three is plenty.
Elsie tells them both they are her favourite people in all Lanternmere, and means it.
Tamsin and Tilly glance at each other, as if checking which of them she meant.
At the quest board the three read the F-rank notices, Cora two steps behind.
Cellar rats, four lanterns; a lost goat in the Underbloom, three; moonbells from the Glasswood, six.
Tilly explains moonbells go into fever draughts; Elsie lights up at that, and Tamsin wants the six.
Tamsin takes down the moonbell notice; they will set out at dawn tomorrow.
Elsie chalks three names and a flower on a slate; Tilly adds a crooked heart, then rubs it out.
Cora writes in her ledger; Elsie asks what she wrote, and Cora closes it.
In the evening the party crosses the canal to the Tipsy Heron, loud and cheap, Cora following.
They each eat a tavern supper at four pips; Tamsin will not let Elsie pay for hers.
Cora sits alone at the next table with a pot of black tea, and does not drink it.
Tamsin tells the Copper Hounds story, loud and funny, until it stops being funny.
Elsie takes her hand across the table and holds it until Tamsin can talk again.
Tilly admits her father thinks she's still at the College; Elsie says they will tell him together.
Glowing, Elsie tells them both, "I love you!" Tamsin chokes on her ale, and Tilly drops her spoon.
Later, low, Tamsin asks if Elsie did something to her with the class, because she feels so strange.
Elsie says no, never, not without asking; Tilly admits she wondered the same thing.
From the next table, without looking up, Cora says Elsie has used no skill all day.
Tamsin and Tilly sit with that, and neither knows whether it makes things better or worse.
Tamsin and Tilly go off to their lodgings, promising to meet at the east gate at dawn.
At dusk Cora walks Elsie home as the lamplighters light the lanterns; it is her duty, she says.
Elsie hums; on a hump-backed bridge she slips, and Cora catches her against her chest.
For a breath Cora holds her, warm and slight, rose-pink hair under her chin, and does not let go.
Then she sets Elsie on her feet and walks on a step ahead, very straight.
At the Honeycomb's door Elsie asks again how Cora takes her tea.
After a long moment Cora says: black, strong, one sugar. Nobody has ever asked her.
Elsie hugs her goodnight; Cora stands stiff in her arms, and her hand lifts, and falls.
Cora walks home toward Wick Lane by way of Lantern Square.
At the Memorial of Strings, Cora touches the bronze threads for her grandmother's family.
In her rooms over the chandler's she opens her ledger and writes: Skills used: none.
Below it she writes: asked how I take my tea. She looks at the line a long while, and leaves it.
In the attic, Elsie tells Mrs Pennywhistle and Captain all about her day.
She hangs her belt, rank tag and all, on the bedpost, then unlaces the halter and undresses.
In her notebook: Tamsin, axe called Margery. Tilly, goggles. Cora: black, strong, one sugar.
She writes to her mother: not a healer's class, but she has friends already, so please don't worry.
She cries a little over the letter, then smiles, and signs it with a flower.
She wishes her window open; under Bonds, where nothing stood this morning, are Tamsin and Tilly.
She doesn't know what the numbers mean; she touches each name and says goodnight to them.
Elsie falls asleep with the window open over Thimble Canal, lantern light swaying on the ceiling.
